findings.where: The EP scorer's weapon terms — `fn()`'s `c('RATIO', i.weapon.ratio), c('DMG', i.weapon.damage)` at bundle line 11184, and the `ratio`/`dmg` cases in `mn()`. Shipped weight profiles `hn` (line 11326): melee-dps RATIO 40, balanced RATIO 20.
findings.siteSays: "Ranked by EP against this set's weights, cap-aware." · melee-dps: "Favours weapon ratio, Strength, Dexterity and Agility." · "Any Slot takes any wearable item — a worn position, not a hand, so weapon damage scores nothing here."
findings.evidence:
RATIO = damage/delay is the only damage term with a non-zero weight anywhere in the five shipped profiles (DMG is a scorable key in `fn()` but carries no weight in any of them), and neither sees the damage bonus. The omission is not small and it is not symmetric between weapon families.

At level 50, +10, main hand, using the measured chain (land 0.5765, main-hand multi-attack 1.520, attack-speed ×1.900, crit factor 1.089, E[rx] 0.967, Offensive ×2.00 — all **M**) and the published 0.8/1.1:

  Cudgel of the Fool   2H 90/52  Dmg Bon 61.9 → 162.4 DPS vs 122.8 without  **+32.3%**
  Earthshaker          2H 74/70  Dmg Bon 50.9 →  99.4 DPS vs  75.2 without  **+32.2%**
  Aldryn / Thelvorn    1H 40/26  Dmg Bon 13.0 → 127.1 DPS vs 110.7 without  **+14.9%**

Those percentages are more robust than they look: swing rate, haste, stance and multi-attack all cancel out of the ratio, so the figure is just B / (1.089·U·E[rx] + 1.1) and survives any reasonable disagreement about attack speed. In your own unit, the bonus adds a **delay-independent** +0.6875 to a two-hander's ratio and +0.50 to a one-hander's whenever delay ≤ 50. Your best two-hander prints ratio 1.731; the term you are not printing is worth another 0.688 of it. Nine of the top ten weapons by modelled main-hand DPS are two-handers, and it is exactly there that the ratio column understates by a third.

The good news, and it is worth saying because it is the part most planners get wrong: **your ordering is not broken.** I ranked all 425 PRIMARY-capable melee weapons in your catalogue at +10 by ratio and by modelled DPS. They agree **9 of 10 in the top ten and 23 of 25 in the top twenty-five** — the audit's figures, reproduced exactly. What ratio cannot do is tell a reader *how much* a swap is worth, or that a two-hander and a one-hander at the same ratio are not the same weapon.

eqlwiki's Game Mechanics page makes the identical argument in prose — "This is a major reason raw Damage / Delay ratio becomes increasingly inadequate for comparing one-handed and two-handed weapons at higher levels" — and offers `Normalized Primary Score = ((2 × Weapon Damage) + Damage Bonus) / Weapon Delay`.
findings.proposedFix:
**Do not fold the bonus into RATIO**, and do not adopt the wiki's normalized score into the ranking either. I tested folding: because the bonus is additive and barely moves with delay, adding it to dmg/delay promotes Rusty Two Handed Hammer 124 places, Abandoned Orc Shovel 133, Micah 148 — ratio stops being even a rough DPS proxy the moment a delay-independent term is inside it.

Instead add `DMG_BONUS` as its own weightable key beside RATIO and DMG, scored only when `weaponCounts` is true (so Any Slot still scores nothing and the existing copy stays true), and ship it at **weight 0** in all five default profiles until someone decides what it is worth. That gives a reader who knows what they are doing a lever, costs a reader who does not exactly nothing, and commits the planner to no DPS claim.

If you ever want a defensible weight: a point of damage bonus is worth roughly 1/2.1 of a point of DMG on the same weapon, because the roll contributes ~2.1×DMG to an average hit while the bonus contributes 1×B. RATIO 40 / DMG_BONUS 19 is internally consistent. That is a derivation and should be badged as one.

And resist the step past it. A DPS number would be the first figure on the site that no source carries and no client window prints — a model output in the same typography as a scraped stat, on a page whose whole argument is that those are different kinds of thing. Note also that `ATTACK` is aggregated by `Kt()` and is structurally always zero: **0 of the 2,263 catalogued items with a slot carry an ATTACK stat** (verified across all 19 shards), so the one stat that would feed a damage model arrives empty. If a DPS screen is ever wanted it belongs on its own page with its own standing — and with the measurement-convention warning attached, because wall-clock, engaged, best-60s and best-30s DPS differ by up to 1.75× on the same fight and four shipped Legends meters use four different denominators.

findings.evidence:
Read from the shipped bundle. `At(e,t)` is `e <= 10 ? e + full : e + Math.floor(e * Ot(t) / 10)`, which is algebraically identical to the `value + max(tier, floor(value·0.1·tier))` rule this project validated — I checked the equivalence in both directions and it holds at every whole tier. `jt(e,t)` is `e + Math.floor(e * Ot(t) / 10)` with no `+1/tier` floor at all.

Your captures confirm the floor for everything except weapon damage. **No capture distinguishes the two rules for weapon damage**, because both captured weapons have base DMG above 10: Whitened Treant Fists 14 → 14/15/16/18 at +0..+3 under either rule, Earthshaker 37 → 74 at +10 under either.

But **265 of the 431 melee weapons in your catalogue — 61.5% — have base DMG below 10** (verified across all 19 shards), and under `jt` their damage does not move at all at +1. Under the floor rule a 9-damage weapon reaches 19 at +10 instead of 18; a 3-damage weapon reaches 13 instead of 6.

The upstream is ambiguous rather than silent, which is why this is worth saying out loud rather than guessing. eqlwiki `Item Upgrade System`, verbatim and live: "A minimum increase of +1 to a stat is guaranteed at the start of each tier" and, in a separate bullet, "Weapon damage is increased at +5% per Tier." So the page states the floor as a rule about *stats* and then carves weapon damage out into its own percentage — leaving exactly the question your two functions answer differently.
findings.proposedFix:
Say the divergence out loud rather than resolve it on suspicion — one line in "What it will not tell you": below 10 base damage a weapon's damage does not move until the percentage clears 1, and whether the +1/tier floor that every other stat obeys also applies here has not been checked.

One client window settles it and it is cheap: **Efreeti Standard at +1 or higher** (3 damage / 10 delay, Plane of Sky cleric quest reward, already in your catalogue as a SECONDARY item). The shipped rule says DMG 3 at +1, +2 and +3; the floor rule says 4, 5, 6. Any sub-10-damage weapon at any tier ≥ 1 does the same job.

Our repo has the mirror of this problem and yours may be the correction: `/home/user/sky-ledger/model4.py` line 67 is `def up10(v): return v+max(10,int(v*0.1*10))`, applied to weapon damage as well as stats — which turns Efreeti Standard into a 13-damage/10-delay off-hand at +10 and forced an empirical `OH_RATE_CAP=1.42` (line 33) to stop the optimiser choosing it. findings.siteSays: settle: "engine/stats.ts takes the maximum; engine/ep.ts adds every haste item at full weight with no cap, so a second haste item earns ranking points for a gain the character will never see." · findings[0]: "Not detected in this build. Either the scorer was fixed or the scanner's pattern no longer matches; check both before believing this line."
findings.evidence:
Read from the shipped bundle rather than the source: **it is fixed.** The EP scorer's haste case routes through

  `function dn(e, t) { let n = Math.max(t, e) - t; return { counted: n, wasted: e - n } }`

called as `dn(t, r.existing?.haste ?? 0)` — `t` the candidate's haste, the second argument the best haste already worn elsewhere in the set, computed by `Wn()` with the candidate's own position excluded. A second haste item scores its excess over the incumbent and nothing more; an equal or lower one scores zero and is reported as `capped`. `Kt()` takes the maximum on the totals side and counts `hasteSources`, and the stat panel prints that only the largest is counted. The two halves of the engine agree.
findings.proposedFix: Change findings[0] from the ambiguous "either the scorer was fixed or the pattern no longer matches" to a positive statement with the evidence — the EP scorer takes the marginal gain over the best worn haste, so the contradiction is closed — and name the function. A scanner that can say "this one is fixed, here is the code" is more persuasive than one that only counts hits, and this is currently the only row on that page you can close. (The separate `haste-pct` signature — what the number *means* — is untouched by this and stays open.)

  · Bone-Clasped Girdle +4 — AC 4→8, HP 75→105, MANA 75→105, STR/STA/DEX 7→11 (6)
  · Bladestopper +6 — AC 25→40, HP 50→80, STA 15→24 (3)
  · Cloak of Flames +7 — AC 10→17, HP 50→85, AGI 9→16, DEX 9→16, **HASTE 36→43**, SV Fire 15→25 (6)
  · Earthshaker +10 — DMG 37→74, STR 6→16, STA 6→16, **SV Void → 10** (4)
  · Whitened Treant Fists +1/+2/+3 — DMG 15, 16, 18 from base 14 (3)

Two rules fall out that nothing else in the field settles. **Haste takes the flat +1/tier rule** (`Mt`), not the scaled one: 36+7=43, where the scaled rule gives 61. Our own EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md, by stating a single blanket upgrade formula, gets that item wrong by +42% — your engine is right and our doc is not. And the **+1/tier floor is confirmed where it actually binds**, in three of the five records and seven fields in total: Bone-Clasped's STR/STA/DEX 7→11 at +4 (percentage gives 9), Cloak's AGI/DEX 9→16 at +7 (gives 15), Earthshaker's STR/STA 6→16 at +10 (gives 12). Earthshaker has the widest margin but it is not the only case, and three independent items is a much better claim than one.

The same captures also refute eqlwiki's `Item Upgrade System` page, live and verbatim: "Weapon damage is increased at +5% per Tier." Whitened Treant Fists at +0/+1/+2/+3 reads 14/15/16/18; +5%/tier predicts 14/14/15/16. The +3 reading refutes it outright — even granting the page's own mid-tier accumulation rule, +5% cannot exceed a 20% cumulative bonus at tier 3, and 18 from a base of 14 requires 28.6%. Your `jt()` ships the winning rule; the site never says that it does, and no page on the site mentions the conflict.
findings.proposedFix:
Split the stats confidence note in two. **Base values:** "match the client on every sample taken so far" (what it says now). **Upgrade curve:** 22 of 22 upgraded fields across five client windows, with the two rules that only these captures settle — the +1/tier floor confirmed on three items where it actually binds, and haste shown to take the flat rule rather than the scaled one. Then one line closing the +5%/tier question: refuted by your own Whitened Treant Fists capture at +3, where no mid-tier accumulation can rescue it.

A worked example on the tools page — a ring that looks better in isolation and scores lower in a set already near the attribute cap — would be the strongest argument for using this planner over any other.

A dry streak is a ceiling, not a zero, and an absent figure is shown as absent rather than reconstructed from a classic formula." The site's read that it is derived from level and weapon type rather than stored per item is confirmed. **The two-handed half validates twice and one of them is the site's own capture.** Earthshaker, cited in its own `sdc` ("observed in a live client window at +10 — Base Dmg 74, Delay 70"): 1.10 × 74 × (50/40) × 0.50 = 50.875 → **50**, client prints **50**. Skycleaver, T2, wikitext fetched 29 Aug (`Skill: 2H Slashing  Atk Delay: 35 | DMG: 30 | Dmg Bon: 24`): 1.10 × 50 × (35/40) × 0.50 = 24.06 → **24**, printed **24**. **The one-handed half does not, and I am reporting that rather than averaging it away.** Both 1H points I can verify come out one low: Whitened Treant Fists 0.69 × 50 × (28/40) × 0.50 = 12.08 against a printed 13; Efreeti Standard (wikitext verified: `Skill: 1H Blunt  Atk Delay: 10 | DMG: 3 | Dmg Bon: 5`) gives 4.31 against a printed 5. Both want HandMod nearer 0.75, but no single rounding rule fits all four points at once — 0.69 with truncation fits the two 2H cases and misses both 1H cases; 0.75 with round-half-up fits both 1H cases and breaks Earthshaker (50.875 → 51 against a printed 50). Two further caveats worth stating: this project's 1H constant of 0.69 was solved from two client windows (Garduk, Arydryidriyorn) that I could not re-check — neither wiki page carries a `Dmg Bon` line, so those captures live outside anything I can see; and every validation point is at level 50, so the `Level/100` term is assumed rather than measured in the level dimension.
findings.proposedFix: I would **not** recommend printing a derived Dmg Bon in every item card yet, and that is a change from how this was first written up. The honest offer is narrower and I think more useful: take the formula as an open derivation to test rather than a number to ship. If you want to act on it now, the defensible subset is two-handers only, where it hits your own Earthshaker capture exactly and Skycleaver exactly, labelled derived rather than sourced. Three things to keep whatever you do with it: (1) it contributes zero from the offhand, and the client prints a Dmg Bon line even on offhand-only items — Efreeti Standard is `sl: ["SECONDARY"]` and shows one — so a naive per-item printout misleads exactly there; (2) the one-handed constant is unresolved between 0.69 and 0.75 and the two checks available both favour the higher value; (3) the point that matters most for your copy is not the number but the shape — the bonus is genuinely not a per-item field and no amount of scraping will find it, so "absent" is the correct state for `wp.bonus` and always will be, which is worth saying outright rather than leaving as a dry streak.

findings.where: Bundle upgrade math: the flat-family list `[HASTE, REGEN, HP_REGEN, MANA REGEN, MANA_REGEN, END_REGEN, ENDUR_REGEN, ATTACK]` routed through a `value + tier` function while attributes, AC, HP, mana and saves take a separate piecewise rule. Affects the 23 rows carrying a HASTE stat.
findings.siteSays: Bundle haste note, verbatim: "The number is the wiki's classic haste field. Whether Legends reads it as a percentage or as a flat attack-speed value is unsettled, so no unit is printed." And on stacking: "Only the highest worn haste counts. They do not add up… Assumed, not measured. Classic EverQuest worked this way and the eqltools Haste Guide says Legends does too — a named community guide, which corroborates rather than observes. No session in this repository has put two hasted items on one character."
findings.evidence: This runs in the site's favour and against this project, so I am filing it as corroboration. The split upgrade rule is **confirmed by the planner's own Tier M capture**. Cloak of Flames is `sd: tier-M` with `sdc`: "observed in a live client window at +7 — AC 17, HP 85, AGI 16, DEX 16, Haste 43, SV Fire 25", against a base of AC 10, HP 50, AGI 9, DEX 9, HASTE 36, SV Fire 15. Six of six predictions land, but only one of them discriminates: AC 10, AGI 9 and DEX 9 are all at or under the piecewise threshold so both rules agree on them, HP 50→85 and SV Fire 15→25 exercise the percentage branch, and **HASTE 36→43 is the single field that proves haste is exempt** — the general rule predicts 61 and the client reads 43, which is base + tier exactly. That is an 18-point discrepancy, so a reader recomputing by hand will conclude the planner is broken. Reading the shipped code confirms the mechanism rather than inferring it: attributes and saves go through a function that is `value + tier` at or below 10 and `value + floor(value × tier / 10)` above it — algebraically identical to this project's `value + max(tier, floor(value×0.1×tier))`, so the two projects agree everywhere except on the flat family. Weapon damage has its own third rule, `value + floor(value × tier / 10)` with no +1 floor, which the Earthshaker capture also confirms (37 → 74 at +10) — worth knowing because it settles a 5%-vs-10%-per-tier conflict this project had flagged as open, in the planner's favour. Correction to us: EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md presents the 10%/tier rule without exception; it was validated on an item with no HASTE, so it was never tested where it fails.
findings.proposedFix: One copy change, no code change: state the split in the upgrade note — attributes, AC, HP, mana and saves take +10% of base per tier with a +1 floor, while HASTE and the regen family take a flat +1 per tier, confirmed against the Cloak of Flames capture. It is worth stating precisely because the gap is large (36 → 43, not 61). I would **leave the haste unit note as "unsettled"**, and this is where I disagree with how this was first drafted: a measured swing-rate multiplier cannot distinguish the two models, because a classic percentage that divides delay and a flat attack-speed stat of 190 against a base of 100 predict the identical rate. This project has an effective attack-speed multiplier of 1.900 measured off one weapon on one character, and a client panel reading `Attack Speed % 100` unhasted, and neither says how an item's haste field maps onto that stat — which is exactly what your own note asks for. The screenshot you are asking for is still the thing that settles it. The non-stacking assumption also stays untested here: no character in this corpus wears two hasted items either.

Check 1 — Earthshaker, from the planner's own `sdc`: "observed in a live client window at +10 — … SV Void 10". Earthshaker carries STR, STA and DEX, so the rule yields 10; the client reads 10. Check 2 — Midnight Clad Straps, from a client tooltip recorded in this project's EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md: at +6 the client reads `SV Void: 6`, and the catalogued base (AC 10, STR/STA/INT/WIS 13) has four qualifying stats, so the rule yields 6. findings.proposedFix: Publish the rule. It is a good piece of reverse-engineering that currently exists only in minified code, and it is exactly the kind of derived-rather-than-sourced number the sources page is scrupulous about labelling everywhere else — a short `dataReliability.voidSave` card stating the rule with the two client checks cited would put it on the same footing. findings.where: 32 rows with `era: "Kunark"` shipping with `av: true`, 28 of them `sd: tier-5`, against the landing copy on /tools/50-upgrades.html §01
findings.siteSays: /tools/50-upgrades.html §01, in full: "It was cut down from 11,252 rows: 7,599 are held back because nothing places them in EverQuest Legends, which is 68 per cent of what it started with, and Kunark, Velious and Luclin are the bulk of it. **3,653 of what survives are here on era alone; the other 10 have no era placing them and are here because something independent proves they exist.**"

In §01, widen the second clause to cover era rank as well as era absence — something like "32 rows sit above the current era and ship anyway, because a live export or a measured drop proves the game has them; they keep their era badge." And on any row whose era ranks above `era.current`, consider pairing the era chip with a short "shipped on Tier M existence evidence" note, since the era chip alone reads as a contradiction rather than as a documented exception. notes:
METHOD. I re-fetched everything rather than trusting the audit: data/meta.json, data/items-index.json, all 19 shards under data/items/ (18 named plus the undocumented OTHER), and the 503KB bundle, on 29 Aug 2026. 4,004 shard rows dedupe to 3,663 unique names; 323 names appear in more than one shard and every duplicate pair is byte-identical. Every published count reproduces exactly (3,663 / 2,263 slotted / 1,713 statted / 538 with effects / 3,456 with acquisition / 299 with an id / 187 era-unknown / 16 statsUnknown / 10 existence-only / 2,045 T2 / 1,487 unattributed / 126 T5 / 5 tier-M). I read the site pages myself (/tools/50-upgrades.html, /sources.html) and pulled the planner's own copy verbatim out of the bundle. I re-parsed the 138 logs and the four inventory exports rather than inheriting any number from this project's markdown. Eleven findings in, eleven out — but four were rewritten, two were rewritten to say the opposite of what they said, and one was replaced entirely.

WHAT I KILLED, AND WHY.

1. "Move Whitened Treant Fists from 1H Blunt to Hand to Hand." Killed as a recommendation. The site already publishes this contradiction in `dataReliability.weaponSkill.clientVerifiedContradictions` and states its reason for not acting: correcting a source on suspicion is the invention its standard exists to prevent. Asking it to act is asking it to change a policy, not to fix an error — that is a scope difference, not a fault. And the log argument is weaker than it was presented. It runs: the logger in e2e-overview.log is Primitive, Primitive's offhand is Whitened Treant Fists, an offhand claw lane exists and no crush lane does, therefore the offhand is not 1H Blunt. I checked each link. The claw lane really is a weapon lane and not the monk Tiger Claw special — across five large logs it runs at 0.42–0.59 attempts/s with a 2s median gap and tracks the slash lane at ~85%, where every genuine special lane (kick, strike, smite) runs at 0.13–0.33/s with 3–5s gaps. Good. But the identification is inferential: `wl44-swap-boundary.log` carries a /who line reading `[50 PAL/MNK/ENC] Primitive (Dark Elf)` and the Aug 01 merge run to Thelvorn +5 / Whitened Treant Fists +4 matches the inventory export exactly, and e2e-overview.log continues that same Thelvorn line to +8 on Aug 05 — so the chain holds, but "Primitive" is a reused fixture name that appears in the corpus across at least nine different class trios and two races, the inventory export and the fight are four days apart, and the corpus contains no line at all linking the Hand to Hand skill to the claw verb (both logs with Hand to Hand skill-ups have zero damage lines). It is real corroborating evidence and I would offer it as that. It is not a second instrument that forces a data change.

2. The proposed replacement of the monk suspect regex with a shape test (MNK-explicit, PRIMARY/SECONDARY, sz TINY/SMALL, wt ≤ 1.0). Killed by running it: it misses Brass Knuckles (sz MEDIUM, wt 1) and picks up Efreeti Scimitar and Fool's Gold Stein. It loses a true suspect and gains two false ones, so it is strictly worse than what ships. Replaced with the thing I did find by running the published rule literally — it selects 5 rows, not the published 4, because "claw" matches inside "Bloodclaw Mace". That is now its own finding, and the fix is one word boundary.

3. "45 of the 48 markup rows are pure duplicates; 3 items would lose their effect if the markup rows were dropped." Both halves wrong, and I checked them because the proposed fix depended on them. All 48 have a same-kind twin carrying the same effect name, so nothing loses an effect. And a dedupe on (k, n, d, lv) after stripping tags collapses only 43 of the 48, because five twins differ in payload — Staff of Writhing's clean twin carries "Rate +75%" the markup row lacks. Shipping the proposed fix as written would have left five items still showing their effect twice and silently discarded a proc rate. The finding survives; the fix changed.

4. "The haste unit note can move from 'unsettled' to 'measured, one reading'." Killed. A classic percentage that divides delay and a flat attack-speed stat of 190 against a base of 100 predict exactly the same swing rate, so this project's measured 1.900 multiplier cannot distinguish them. The site's note is correct as it stands and asks for precisely the thing that would settle it. Recommending it downgrade "unsettled" on this evidence would be the error the brief warns about, and the surviving finding says so.

5. "Runed Bolster Belt is the strongest ALL-class haste recommendation in the planner and it rests on tier-5 Kunark numbers." Killed. Haste is max-only and Cloak of Flames (BACK, ALL classes, HASTE 36, sd tier-M) beats its 31 for every class, so the Kunark row contributes nothing to anyone who has one. It is the best ALL-class *waist* haste and nothing more. The era/prose mismatch survives on its own merits at low impact.

6. All minified identifier attributions — `Ut`, `Nt`, `Kt`, `Zn`, `qt`, `Gt`, `It`, `Mt(e.wp.dmg,t)`. None of them match the bundle actually served at that URL; the flat-stat family is `Ht`, the void qualifier is `Ut`, the aggregator is `Kt`, weapon damage goes through its own function and not the flat one. The behaviour claims all held up when I read the code, so I have cited by content and quoted the code fragments I could verify verbatim (`weaponCounts: n===\`PRIMARY\`||n===\`SECONDARY\``, `o>t.haste&&(t.haste=o)`, `t.attack+=e.flat.ATTACK??0`, `OFFHAND:\`SECONDARY\``).

7. Several count claims, corrected in place rather than dropped: "22 Replaced-with cases" is 23 (one carries the reason on the following line); "wp.skillRaw on 1 row" is 12 rows, eleven of which are Throwing normalisations working correctly; the Kunark ex breakdown is 12/11/9, not 13/11/8; the inventory-export join gives 358 names / 165 fillable ids / 92 promotions / 56 unmatched on my parse against the audit's 233/108/70/33, and I have said so and stated my parse rule, because the difference is bag and keyring rows.

THE ONE THING THAT CHANGED A FIX RATHER THAN A NUMBER. The Delete-template finding is the biggest one and it nearly went out with the wrong remedy. The proposal was to quarantine the 112 rows whose wiki pages read "not relevent in EQ legends". I ran the absence check the site's own standard demands and found a counterexample: `Small Ringmail Belt` carries that exact annotation and a Legends combat log dated 2 August 2026 shows it being looted four times, once as `Small Ringmail Belt +1` with the Legends-only upgrade suffix. The wiki annotation is wrong about at least one of the 145. So the template has to be a review flag, never a filter — which is also the right tier answer, since the reason string is editorial wiki prose and not structured data. The finding is stronger for it, and the fix now leads with the 23 supersession pairs, which are the half where the wiki names its own replacement and the replacement is already in the catalogue.

THREE THINGS THAT CORRECT US RATHER THAN THE SITE, and which I have kept in the findings so the owner is not asked to fix our mistakes. HASTE and the regen family take a flat +1 per tier, not the 10% rule EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md presents without exception — and the planner's own Cloak of Flames capture proves it (36 → 43, not 61). The catalogue does carry base SV Void on two rows, against EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md's "knows only the classic five", and it derives the rest by a rule that validates 2/2. And the planner's weapon-damage rule of 10% per tier is confirmed by its own Earthshaker capture (37 → 74 at +10), which settles a 5%-vs-10% conflict this project had flagged as open, in the site's favour.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY AND AM NOT CLAIMING. Whether the 92 `Piercing` rows are one- or two-handed in Legends — several are LARGE PRIMARY-only spears and the corpus cannot settle it; the proposed fix is a vocabulary rename that moves no weapon between skills. Whether worn haste stacks — no character in this corpus wears two hasted items, so the corpus could not have contained the answer, and the planner says so itself. Whether Legends gates dual wield by class — genuinely unsettled, and deliberately excluded from the two-hander fix. The 1H damage-bonus constant of 0.69, which was solved in this project from two client windows (Garduk, Arydryidriyorn) I could not re-check: neither wiki page carries a Dmg Bon line, so those captures are outside anything I can see, and both 1H points I *can* verify come out one low against it. And the "2 of 11,534 wiki items carry ATTACK" figure, which is this project's T2 census carried over rather than re-derived here — I verified only the catalogue-side zero.

TONE NOTE FOR WHOEVER SENDS THIS. This catalogue is unusually careful. It grades its own rows, publishes the grades, names four failure modes against itself, prints the suspect rule on screen so a reader can check it, and refuses to correct a source on suspicion. Three of the eleven findings are corroborations or corrections to us. Of the two that matter most, one is the deleted-pages signal — genuinely absent, genuinely cheap, and with a counterexample attached that says use it as a flag — and the other is the two-hander interaction, where the slot legality underneath is already perfect and only the interaction between two correct slots is missing. Nothing here is a criticism of the standard; most of it is the standard applied one step further out.

findings.where: /learn/still-true.html — entry "Is haste a percentage, or a flat attack-speed value?" (graded Open), section "What Legends does"; and the identical framing in /learn/contamination.html, "Mechanics we know changed", row haste-pct
findings.siteSays: still-true.html: "The two best sources in this community disagree, and we were republishing one of them without noticing. EQL Tools states that slow and haste in Legends are flat values on an attack-speed stat — a mob at 100 attack speed with 60 haste sits at 160, and the numbers add rather than compounding. eqlwiki's own Haste Guide, edited 4 August 2026, still carries the classic percentage formula and cites classic-era raid content around it." contamination.html, row haste-pct: "Legends: Legends uses a flat value on an attack-speed stat. EQL Tools documents it; eqlwiki still carries the classic formula, so the two best sources in the field disagree."
findings.evidence: Both halves of the quotation are accurate; the conclusion drawn from them is not. The two sources do not disagree, and I checked this on the site's own two citations. (a) T3, EQL Tools' OTHER page, eqltools.com/learn/combat, "Haste" section, verbatim: "Haste cuts your weapon delay up to a cap that rises with level. Your stat window prints your current Haste and its cap on their own rows [client-mined] — trust that number at your level over any rule of thumb." and "Players put the level-50 cap at about 75% haste — 175% swing speed — reachable without buffs". That is the delay-cutting percentage model, on EQL Tools, with the same 75% cap eqlwiki gives. (b) T5, eqlwiki Haste Guide (our copy, footer "last edited on 4 August 2026, at 12:17" — the same read the site dates) says in its own Haste Rules list: "Haste is measured in Rate of Attack Increase, NOT Delay Decrease", then gives Delay/(1+Haste) as the equivalent delay computation, and carries a Legends-authored caps table (1-30: 55%, 31-50: 75% "Gain 1% max per level after 30", 51-60: 100% "Will need to test once available!") plus Legends-only content ("Currently, the Magician's Frenzied Burnout is the only source of 'overhaste' in Everquest Legends", "[per Embrwo, 07/04/26]"). Levels 51-60 do not exist in Legends, so that row cannot be a P99 import. (c) The two formulas are the same arithmetic for swing rate: delay/(1+h) gives 10(1+h)/delay swings/s; attack speed 100 -> 160 gives x1.60. For h=60% both give x1.60 on every weapon. (d) Tier M, our client character panel read verbatim off one unbuffed character: `HP Regen 16  Mana Regen 34  End Regen 23  Attack Speed %  100` — the stat exists, is named Attack Speed, is printed with a percent sign, and reads 100 unhasted. (e) T2, eqlwiki's structured spell effect field writes Legends haste as a percent on that same stat: 52 occurrences of "Increase Attack Speed by N%" across the 2,006-spell harvest, e.g. Alacrity "Increase Attack Speed by 34% (L24) to 40% (L36)"; the Bard class page {{RadSpellRow2}} `max=` column writes a slow as "-25% Atkspd". Where the sources genuinely differ is stacking: eqlwiki Haste Guide prose says "For haste items, only the item with highest haste % counts. [per Embrwo, 07/04/26]", EQL Tools says "Haste sources stack only up to the cap" and "Three buckets that stack: item + spell + overhaste." That is a real, narrow, testable disagreement — and it is not the one the entry names.
findings.proposedFix: Retitle from "percentage or flat" to something like "Do haste sources stack, and what is the cap?", and rewrite "What Legends does" so it stops asserting a disagreement that the site's own two citations do not contain. The units half is settled and can be stated: Legends' stat is called Attack Speed, its unhasted baseline is 100, it is printed in percent, so a "+41%" figure is Legends' own unit and not a classic import. Then keep two genuinely open lines: (a) the cap — eqlwiki's Legends-authored caps table and EQL Tools' "about 75% at 50, 175% swing speed" agree, so this is close to settled at T3/T5 and wants one client reading; (b) stacking — eqlwiki says highest worn item only, EQL Tools says item + spell stack up to the cap, and those two really do conflict. Same edit applies to the contamination haste-pct row. Note also that the 50 Upgrades planner already frames this better than this page does ("the eqltools Haste Guide describes flat attack-speed values under a level-scaled cap, while eqlwiki still documents its own item field as 'worn haste %'"), so the two surfaces currently disagree with each other.

findings.where: /learn/still-true.html — haste entry, the "What would settle it" sentence
findings.siteSays: "What would settle it. One screenshot of a Legends haste item tooltip. If it reads a bare number rather than a percentage, EQL Tools is right and every percentage figure on this site is a classic import."
findings.evidence: The test's premise is false on EQL Tools' own pages, so it cannot come out the way it is written, and acting on it would mark correct Legends data as classic contamination. T3, eqltools.com/learn/control, "Haste" section, verbatim with its own source badges: "Total haste is capped around 50% below level 30 and about 75% at 50.[dev] Item haste alone reaches the cap — a dev cited an upgraded 41% item plus a clicky or proc[dev]". The link title attribute on that badge reads "Dev-stated: an upgraded 41% item and a clicky or proc reaches the cap." EQL Tools also writes "Largo's Melodic Binding is the AE at 35%; its stronger 40% slow" and "Berserker Stance ... players put it at +100%". So EQL Tools writes haste in percent throughout and attributes a 41% item to a developer. A tooltip reading "+41%" is therefore fully consistent with EQL Tools being right about everything it actually claims; the tooltip's unit is not diagnostic. findings.proposedFix: Replace the settling test. The unit question is answered; what is unresolved is stacking, and that is what a screenshot can settle. The planner already names a workable one-item version, verbatim: "One screenshot settles it: a Legends item tooltip showing its haste line beside the character's Attack Speed reading, on a character wearing that item and nothing else hasted." The two-item version separates the stacking models outright: read Attack Speed with one hasted item worn, then with a second. Additive gives 100+41+21 = 162, highest-only gives 141, compounding gives 100 x 1.41 x 1.21 = 171 — far enough apart that one screenshot pair decides it, and it is the question eqlwiki and EQL Tools actually disagree about.

findings.where: /tools/50-upgrades.html — section 03 "What it will not tell you", the damage-bonus bullet; and the planner's own stat card copy
findings.siteSays: Page, verbatim: "Damage bonus is absent. A client window shows one, no source carries it per item, and it appears to be derived from level and weapon type rather than stored on the item." Planner bundle, verbatim: "The live client shows a Dmg Bon line and no source in this project carries it per item, so this planner prints nothing there. A dry streak is a ceiling, not a zero, and an absent figure is shown as absent rather than reconstructed from a classic formula."
findings.evidence: Two sources carry it per item, and one of them is this site. T2 — eqlwiki's {{Itempage}} stat block prints a literal `Dmg Bon:` / `DMG Bonus:` line, present on 24 of the 11,534 harvested item records (harvest 2026-08-22): skycleaver DMG 30 / delay 35 / Dmg Bon 24; efreeti zweihander 24 / 45 / 30; efreeti standard 3 / 10 / 5; whitened treant fists 14 / 28 / 13; blade of abrogation 20 / 39 / 19; and 19 more. On the derivation the page's own guess is right, and the two-handed half is tightly pinned: at level 50 all six in-era two-handed rows are reproduced exactly by round(delay x 0.675) — 28→19, 30→20, 35→24, 35→24, 36→24, 45→30 — which is HandMod x max(50,DMG) x (min(delay,50)/40) x (Level/100) with HandMod constrained to [1.074, 1.084]. The one-handed half is NOT pinned and I am not proposing a constant for it: the 16 in-era 1H rows are mutually inconsistent (delay 28 → 13 requires HandMod < 0.771, delay 30 → 15 requires HandMod >= 0.773), the best single value reproduces 13 of 16, and this project's own Tier M figure of 0.69 — taken from two client windows whose parse I could not locate in the repo — reproduces 1 of 16. findings.proposedFix: Change §03 from "no source carries it" to what is true: eqlwiki's item stat block carries Dmg Bon on 24 items, 19 of which are already in the planner's catalogue, and the planner can print those at T2 today with no derivation at all. For two-handers beyond those, a derived figure badged derived is defensible and the derivation can be named — a fit to six Legends rows, exact on all six, not the classic level/delay table the copy rightly refuses to import. For one-handers, print nothing and say why: the wiki's own rows cannot all be true of one constant. Flag `the butcherblock hammer` (Dmg Bon 113) as a suspect source value, and re-read Cudgel of the Fool.

findings.where: /sources.html — change log, 14 Aug 2026, entry "Our verified tier was carrying classic data", and the same claim in the 14 Aug contamination entry
findings.siteSays: "An outside audit found six Plane of Sky reward tooltips carrying percentage haste — five of them the identical +41%, which is a copied constant and not five readings. Legends uses a flat attack-speed value. All six sat under classes the tracker flagged verified."
findings.evidence: The transcription is faithful and the copied-constant charge does not hold. (a) +41% is not a Sky-family duplication: it appears on 20 of the 11,534 harvested eqlwiki item records, across four era tags (Sky, Kunark, Velious, FearHateRevamp) and on head, waist, back, feet, hands and weapon slots — it behaves like the game's maximum item-haste value, not like a stamped copy. (b) The value is dev-attributed: EQL Tools, eqltools.com/learn/control, badges it "dev" — "a dev cited an upgraded 41% item plus a clicky or proc". (c) eqlwiki carries the six independently in two unrelated structures: the {{Itempage}} `stats` field on each item, and the Haste Guide's Permanent Haste Items table, which lists Belt of the Four Winds, Girdle of Faith and Golden Sash of Tranquility at 41% and Honeycomb Belt at 26%, each with its own condensed stat summary and its own quest attribution ("Warrior Test of Think", "Paladin Test of Spirit", "Monk Test of Tranquility", "Druid Test of the Bee"). The sixth member of the family carrying a different number in both structures is the opposite of a stamped constant. (d) Two of the six cannot be Project 1999 imports at all: diaphonous waistband is BST and sash of ferocity is BER, and Project 1999 has neither class; both also carry the Legends-native flag wording "Lore Equipped, No Trade" rather than the classic "MAGIC ITEM LORE ITEM NO DROP" the other four use. (e) The premise "Legends uses a flat attack-speed value", used here as grounds for suspecting a percentage, does not do that work — see the two haste findings above.
findings.proposedFix: Re-label the six from "suspect transcription" to something like "matches eqlwiki's item record field for field, and matches eqlwiki's Haste Guide table independently; the value itself has not been read off a Legends client." That keeps the honest residue — nobody has inspected these in game, which is also what /sources.html §02 says under "Five class tooltips" — and drops the classic-import charge, which the evidence does not support. Worth noting in the same edit that the audit finding you accepted was itself wrong; that is the sort of correction this change log is unusually good at making.

findings.where: /sources.html — section 01 The hierarchy, the Tier 2 definition (and worth repeating on /data/index.html)
findings.siteSays: "Tier 2 — Structured wiki data. Infoboxes, NPC tables, item tables, coordinate records on eqlwiki. Machine-shaped fields that somebody entered from the live game."
findings.evidence: Two cases where the shape of the field does not settle its standing, and both are on eqlwiki. (i) T2 against T2, 7.1x apart, on Bard's three passive PB AE songs. The spell pages' structured effect rows read "Decrease Hitpoints by 2 per tick" (Chords of Dissonance), "4 per tick" (Denon's Disruptive Discord), "2 per tick" (Selo's Chords of Cessation) = 8/tick. The Bard class page's {{RadSpellRow2}} `max=` column, under a header literally reading "Max Effect", gives -14, -16 and -27 HP/tick = 57/tick. Neither page states the level its figure applies to, and the two cannot be reconciled as base-versus-level-60 either: on the same song, the spell page's own scaling notation says "Decrease Attack Speed by 17% (L48) to 20% (L60)" while the class page's max column says "-25% Atkspd". So the spell-page field can express level scaling, does so for AC and attack speed, and does not for the hitpoint lines — and where both fields do carry a maximum, they disagree by 25%. A scraper reading spell pages is out by 7x on the damage and does not know it. (ii) A structured container holding classic prose. AE target caps live in the spell page's `description =` template parameter, not in the slot rows — 10 of 34 AE spells at level <=50 state one: "up to 4 creatures in the vicinity of your target" (Column of Lightning), "up to 8 enemies" (Denon's Desperate Dirge), "up to 25 nearby creatures" (Earthquake), "as many as 24 others nearby" (Tremor), "Outdoors only" and "a full quad" (Lightning Blast). Most scrapes drop that parameter, so the cap is invisible downstream. But the parameter is prose, and several of those pages open with <noinclude>{{Classic Era}}</noinclude> — Column of Lightning, Gravity Flux, Lightning Strike and Pillar of Fire among them. So the caps are simultaneously the most useful field on the page and a tier-5 sentence sitting inside a machine-shaped parameter.
findings.proposedFix: Add one line under Tier 2: a structured field is a container, not a provenance. The tier attaches to the named field, not to the fact that a field exists — so a citation says which field on which page, a base value and a maximum are two different citations, and a template parameter whose contents are prose is tier 5 however machine-shaped its wrapper. That is the exact mirror of the sentence the site already has on /learn/still-true.html ("a tier 5 sentence inside a tier 2 container is the most dangerous object in this ecosystem") — this is the same object one layer down, in the data rather than in the narrative. Worth repeating on /data/index.html, since the whole point of publishing machine-readable data is that other people's scrapers will read one field and not the other.

findings.where: /learn/contamination.html — "Classic formats" table, row sv-resist (217 unmarked, 9 marked)
findings.siteSays: "Classic: Classic stat blocks abbreviated resists as SV MAGIC +N. Legends: The abbreviation may well be current. Its presence marks a block transcribed from a classic-era record, which is worth knowing even when the number is right. What would settle it: Compare one block against the item in game."
findings.evidence: The comparison has been made and the answer is not about the abbreviation. Tier M — a Legends client item tooltip for a +6 Midnight Clad Straps reads `SV Void: 6`, and a Legends character panel prints `SV Void 111` alongside the classic five. The abbreviation style is unchanged; the resist list is not. T2 — eqlwiki's item catalogue carries `SV VOID` on exactly 2 of 11,534 records (anthemion armbands +2, darkspun shroud +1) against `SV MAGIC` on 1,298, so wiki item data is effectively blind to it. Your own planner already models it and validates the rule: the bundle carries an `SV_VOID` key labelled "Void Resist" and grants Void equal to the upgrade tier, with a tier-M provenance note reading "observed in a live client window at +10 — Base Dmg 74, Delay 70, Ratio 1.057, Strength 16, Stamina 16, SV Void 10. Nine of nine predictions exact." Scope caveat, stated so the row is worded accurately: on this evidence Void is mostly granted by the upgrade rather than carried on the base item, so a five-resist block on a +0 item is complete — what is short a field is the character sheet, any upgraded item, and any item comparison run on resists.
findings.proposedFix: Keep the row but change what it tests for. The abbreviation is current and can stop being counted as a marker on its own. The useful signature is the missing sixth: Legends has a resist called Void that the classic five-resist convention cannot express, it appears on upgraded items as a function of tier and on at least two base items, and it shows on the character panel. That moves the row from "conventions rather than errors" to a specific, checkable statement, and it lets you cross-link the planner rule that already predicts it.

findings.where: /learn/contamination.html — "Classic formats" table, row nodrop (65 unmarked, 1 marked), against /learn/still-true.html (epic entry) and /tools/50-upgrades.html §03

What would settle it: One screenshot of an item tooltip carrying the flag." Three spellings of one idea coexist in the source, and Attunable and Lore Equipped have no classic equivalent at all, so one of the two conventions is Legends-native and identifiable by name. findings.proposedFix: Change "Unchecked" to the answer, with the counts, and cross-link the epic entry that supplied it: Legends prints No Trade / Lore Equipped / Attunable; eqlwiki's item field carries both conventions in the proportions above; a block using NO DROP / Lore Item is a transcription marker rather than a current flag. findings.where: /tools/50-upgrades.html — sections 01 and 02, where the planner's upgrade arithmetic is used but carries no source badge (the tools index describes it as "Every item upgrades from +0 to +10 and the stat sheet recomputes as you touch it")
findings.siteSays: /tools/index.html: "Every item upgrades from +0 to +10 and the stat sheet recomputes as you touch it." §02 grades every stat value by source and publishes the counts; the upgrade rules themselves — three separate functions in the bundle — carry no standing on a page whose whole argument is that every number carries one.
findings.evidence: Tier M — a Legends client tooltip for a +6 Midnight Clad Straps (catalogued AC 10, STR 13, STA 13, INT 13, WIS 13) reads AC 16, STR 20, STA 20, INT 20, WIS 20, and `SV Void: 6`. That validates the attribute/AC rule v + max(tier, floor(v x tier / 10)) 5 for 5, including both awkward cases — AC 10 at +6, where the +1-per-tier floor and the 10% tie, and STR 13 at +6, where 10% wins at 7 — plus the Void-equals-tier rule 1 for 1. Separately, the weapon-damage rule is settled by evidence the site already holds and has not published against the conflict: the bundle's own tier-M record for Earthshaker (base DMG 37, delay 70) reads "observed in a live client window at +10 — Base Dmg 74, Delay 70, Ratio 1.057, Strength 16, Stamina 16, SV Void 10. Nine of nine predictions exact." 37 -> 74 is +10% of base per tier; +5% per tier would give 55. eqlwiki's Item Upgrade System page says +5% (T2), and EQL Tools lists the same conflict as open on its own upgrades page, verbatim: "Weapon damage per tier: the wiki says +5%, this site's tools use +10%. One weapon read at two tiers settles it." Your Earthshaker window is that reading.
findings.proposedFix: Publish the three rules on the page with the client tooltip and the Earthshaker window as their standing — they are currently the only arithmetic in the tool with no source badge. And rather than recording the +5% vs +10% weapon-damage question as merely open, publish it as closed by your own tier-M row, against a named T2 page and a named T4 aggregator that both still list it as unsettled. That is a contribution outward rather than a correction inward, and it is the site's own convention to show the disagreement rather than hide it.

findings.where: /learn/reading-the-plans.html — "What a combat log can and cannot tell you"; and /learn/difficulty.html, beside "The ramp, measured on one boss at all five tiers"
findings.siteSays: reading-the-plans.html: "Damage figures describe one party, at one level, against those mobs. A different level or a different trio changes all of them." difficulty.html: "Damage to kill counts every attacker, so read these as what the fight costs a raid rather than what one party deals."
findings.evidence: Both cautions cover the numerator and neither covers the denominator. Re-run by me on the committed corpus (tools/convention.py over the 138 fixture logs, 29 logs with enough damage events to qualify): median best-60s / engaged = 1.23, best-30s / engaged = 1.47, best-10s / engaged = 2.06. Single-log spreads are wider — jos437-finishing-blow reads 265 wall-clock, 483 engaged, 678 over its best 30 s. Four shipped Legends meters use four different denominators by default, and nothing in a quoted number says which. Scope, stated honestly: the string "DPS" does not appear on any eqlsource page I fetched, so this is not a correction to anything you publish — the exposure is a reader's own arithmetic. Your difficulty tables put damage to kill and fight seconds side by side (D4 Master Yael, 234,249–242,060 over 587s), and dividing them gives 412, a raid-wide wall-clock rate that will not match any meter's default reading of the same fight. Correcting the audit that raised this: these ratios are measured per log file rather than per fight — the tool aggregates every engaged segment in a file — so "on the same fight" overstates it slightly.
findings.proposedFix: One bullet on "What a combat log can and cannot tell you": a damage rate needs its denominator named — wall-clock, engaged, or a best-N-second window — and on this corpus the three differ by 1.2x to 2.0x on the same log. One clause beside the difficulty ramp table saying the seconds column is fight duration, and that dividing by it gives a raid-wide wall-clock rate rather than anything a meter will print.

notes:
HOW I CHECKED. I read /sources.html (tier definitions, known gaps, full change log), /learn/index.html, /learn/still-true.html, /learn/contamination.html, /learn/difficulty.html, /learn/motes.html, /tools/50-upgrades.html and the 503KB planner bundle from the local copies, and fetched /learn/raid-access.html and /learn/reading-the-plans.html fresh (the local set did not contain them; the audit claimed to have read them in full and I could not confirm that from what was on disk). Every site quotation above I re-read in the fetched page. On our side I re-ran two measurements rather than citing them: tools/convention.py over the 138 fixture logs, and an independent split-half proc test I wrote. I re-derived the Dmg Bon fit, the haste-item counts, the flag counts and the save counts directly from the 11,534-record eqlwiki harvest.

KILLED — 1. THE PROC-PER-SWING CONTAMINATION ROW (audit finding 6). Proposed adding a second row to "Mechanics we know changed", whose stated meaning on that page is "a hit here is probably a wrong number, because the mechanic it describes demonstrably works differently in Legends". Our supporting evidence is dLogLik +8.19, cross-file CV 0.324 vs 0.396, and a -0.03 correlation — all quoted in DAMAGE-CHAIN.md without a runnable parse, and the CV margin is thin. I built the discriminating test myself: for each proc name, split its engaged segments at the median swing rate and compare PPM stability against per-swing stability. It does not support the claim. Smiting Strike, by far the largest sample (91 segments, 616 fires): swing rate x1.96 between halves, PPM x1.60, per-swing x0.81 — per-swing is the MORE stable of the two. Condemnation of Nife and Cobra Venom Strike go the same way; Lifetap Strike, Dismiss Undead and Drain Spirit go the other. Four to three with the biggest sample against us is not "demonstrably". Handing this to a site with a strict standard, on a page that already carries exactly one row and guards it carefully, would have been the single most damaging thing in the brief.

KILLED — 2. THE PET-TANKING PARAGRAPH (audit finding 11). The 1,318-to-59 figure reproduces in direction — restricting attacker to named and raid bosses I get 617 melee attempts at the player and 1 at anything else — and the corpus can contain the counter-evidence, since it logs 35 hits on Dranix, 27 on Rykkerr and so on. But pets appear in only 11 of 138 logs, and nothing establishes that a pet was ever on a boss with taunt up. "The log owner took the boss melee in these fights" is what was measured; "a pet cannot hold a boss" is an aggro mechanic, and the gap between them is the whole claim. Offering it as new content on a site that publishes nothing about pets would put an unverified mechanic under their badge.

DOWNGRADED — THE 1H DAMAGE-BONUS "CORRECTION TO US". The audit proposed moving this project's HandMod from 0.69 to ~0.76 on the strength of 16 eqlwiki rows. I have not carried that. Three reasons. It inverts the site's own hierarchy (our 0.69 is badged Tier M; the wiki rows are T2). The two client windows behind 0.69, named in DAMAGE-CHAIN.md as Garduk and Arydryidriyorn, have no parse I could find anywhere in the repo or scratchpad — a measurement cited without its parse. And the 16 rows cannot all be true of any single constant: delay 28 -> 13 requires HandMod < 0.771 while delay 30 -> 15 requires HandMod >= 0.773. So the honest statement is that the 1H constant is unresolved on both sides, and finding 3 now says exactly that instead of proposing a number. The two-handed half is different and I did carry it: HandMod is constrained to [1.074, 1.084] by six exact rows, our 1.10 misses three of the six (not two, as the audit said), and 1.08 fits all six.

CORRECTED — A FABRICATED QUOTE IN THE AUDIT. Finding 2 attributed to the planner: "One screenshot settles it: a character's Attack Speed reading with two hasted items worn, beside the same reading with one." The bundle does not say that. It says: "One screenshot settles it: a Legends item tooltip showing its haste line beside the character's Attack Speed reading, on a character wearing that item and nothing else hasted." A one-item calibration, not a stacking test. My finding 2 quotes the real sentence and offers the two-item version as an addition rather than as something they already wrote.

CORRECTED — THE AUDIT'S OWN NEAR-MISS NOTE WAS HALF WRONG. It recorded that the Haste Guide's 16%/21% Plane of Sky belts are different items from the site's class-quest rewards, and killed the apparent conflict. The identity check holds — Belt of Concordance, Belt of Iniquity, Belt of the Pine and Belt of Virtue are random drops at 16%, distinct from the quest rewards. But the audit missed that the same Haste Guide table ALSO lists Belt of the Four Winds, Girdle of Faith, Golden Sash of Tranquility at 41% and Honeycomb Belt at 26%, each with its own quest attribution. That is independent corroboration, and it is now the strongest single leg of finding 4.

NOT USED AS EVIDENCE ANYWHERE, DELIBERATELY. Our headline haste measurement — 1.111 attempts/s on an identified delay-26 main hand over 395s, giving an effective attack-speed multiplier of 1.900 — is unattributed and I would not put it in front of the site owner. It sits above the 1.75 ceiling both eqlwiki and EQL Tools give for level 50, the jos437 log contains no player haste buff or stance line at all, and 1.900 is also precisely our measured berserker-stance rate multiplier. It may be measuring stance rather than haste. It separates none of the haste models and should not be quoted as though it does. Related: SOURCING.md §2 re-anchors the project's haste constant on this number and describes eqlwiki's Haste Guide as carrying "the exact classic percentage-divides-delay formula the scanner flags" — that characterisation does not survive reading the page, which states "Haste is measured in Rate of Attack Increase, NOT Delay Decrease" and carries a Legends-authored caps table including a 51-60 row. That is our error, not the site's, and it is worth fixing on our side before we send anything.

ALSO CHECKED AND CLEAN, so nobody re-runs it. The difficulty page already carries this project's own retraction verbatim. The multiclass-trash-at-D1 observation, the loot-floor rule and the zone-line reading hold against our logs. The trio claims are not testable from our corpus and I assert nothing. The motes ladder and Void Gem advice are T3 and untouched. The 23-slot / no-Charm-slot model in the planner matches our /outputfile ladder exactly. The 10 August change-log rows about the eleven-dungeon placeholder claim are superseded in place by the 18 and 23 August corrections above them, which is the site's stated practice rather than a fault. /learn/raid-access.html's note that measured fights name more than eight attackers is one we can neither confirm nor refute — our parser cannot separate pets from players by name either, exactly as the page says. None of the seven gaps on /sources.html §02 is closable from 138 combat logs and an item harvest; the gaps this contribution closes are the ones stated in place on the Learn and Tools pages.

ONE SMALL THING FOR OUR OWN NOTES, NOT FOR THE SITE. The brief lists Tremor at target cap 25. Its description field reads "as many as 24 others nearby"; Earthquake is the one that reads 25.

findings.siteSays: Anthemion: "Beastlord only · 2 recorded — Dropped by An abhorrent, An ire ghast — The Plane of Hate. findings.where: /learn/difficulty — "Loot gives a third reading, and difficulty is a floor"

findings.evidence: TIER M. The advice is correct; the gap is that the client prints loot in four grammatical forms and this is the only one the site quotes anywhere. findings.proposedFix: Add the loot-line grammar to /learn/difficulty or a short /learn page of its own: the four dispositions, that all of them name the mob and carry the dropped +N, and that the autosell line is where most drops go. findings.where: /learn/difficulty — "Loot gives a third reading, and difficulty is a floor"

findings.evidence: TIER M, independent corpus, and the rule holds cleanly. On 459 deduplicated upgradeable drops carrying a known zone tier: zero below the floor, 58 above = 12.6%, which lands on your "about 12%". (Raw, before removing overlapping fixture copies: 570 drops, 70 above, 12.3%.) The pooled figure hides a gradient worth publishing: D0 34/142 = 23.9%, D1 19/84 = 22.6%, D2 3/105 = 2.9%, D3 2/48 = 4.2%, D4 0/80 = 0.0%. No dropped item anywhere in the corpus exceeds +4 (dropped distribution +0 1119, +1 171, +2 147, +3 57, +4 110), while merged values reach +8 in a `You have successfully merged two items together to create a new item: Thelvorn, Blade of Light +8` line and +9 in the inventory dumps. Your "three drops settle it" advice survives the gradient: at D0, the worst tier for it, the floor value still turns up 76.1% of the time, so three drops identify the tier 98.6% of the time. One caution against overclaiming: that +4 is the highest value ever seen to drop is measured, but that it is a *design* ceiling is not separable from D4 being the current maximum tier, since +5 could only ever arrive as an above-floor roll at D4.
findings.proposedFix: Keep the 12% headline and add the per-tier row, plus one sentence that +4 is the highest value yet seen to drop — so a Refined run shows a pure +4 column and a reader should not read that uniformity as uncertainty. findings.where: /learn/difficulty — "Reading it — the game tells you, twice", against the "Hit points, D1 and D2" and "Experience" rows
findings.siteSays: "Zoning in prints the tier as a number and a name in the same line: You have entered Befallen 1 (Awakened). … A zone line with no number and no name is base difficulty — the open world, or an instance run at base." And in the scaling rows: "×1.15 and ×1.30 on multiplayer tuning, ×1.10 and ×1.20 solo"; "×1.15 / ×1.30 / ×1.45 / ×1.60 … on multiplayer tuning; ×1.10 / ×1.20 / ×1.30 / ×1.40 solo."
findings.evidence: TIER M. The zone line carries a third token this page never shows: a party-size infix between the zone name and the tier. In the corpus: "You have entered Nagafen's Lair - Solo 2 (Adaptive).", "You have entered Nagafen's Lair - Group 3 (Fused).", "You have entered The Plane of Hate - Solo 4 (Refined).", "You have entered The Permafrost Caverns - Solo.", "You have entered The Ruins of Old Paineel - Solo 1 (Awakened)." — 55 such lines, Solo 52 and Group 3 (my first pass said 53/50/3; recounted). The page's rule for the bare form still holds — "- Solo." with no number is an instance at base, and treating those rows as tier 0 produced zero floor violations — so nothing here is wrong. The gap is that the page splits every scaling figure into "multiplayer tuning" and "solo" columns without telling the reader the zone line already carries a Solo/Group token. The site parses it elsewhere: sightings.v1.json sessions carry `"zone": "Nagafen's Lair - Group"`, /sets/ prints "The Plane of Hate - Group", and /tools/faction-impact.html lists "Kedge Keep - Group", "The Permafrost Caverns - Group" and others. One stated limit: that the Solo/Group token is what selects between the two scaling columns is my inference, not something I measured, and EQL Tools' "solo tuning" may not be the same axis — so the page should present the token, not assert the mapping. Two parser traps worth a sentence: " - " is not a safe delimiter ("You have entered Neriak - Foreign Quarter." and "Neriak - Commons." are ordinary zone names), and "You have entered an area where levitation effects do not function." matches the zone-line pattern exactly and fires 15 times in this corpus.

notes:
METHOD. I re-fetched every page under audit live from eqlsource.com on 29 Aug 2026 (byte-identical to the local copies, so those were current), re-downloaded zones.v1.json, items.v1.json and sightings.v1.json, re-queried eqlwiki via api.php for wikitext and category membership, read the 50 Upgrades bundle, and re-derived every corpus number myself from the 138 logs and four /outputfile dumps rather than accepting the audit's. Repo files read first: SOURCING.md, then DAMAGE-CHAIN.md and EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md as needed.

ONE CORPUS-WIDE CORRECTION THAT TOUCHES SEVERAL FIGURES. The fixture set contains overlapping copies: five files are byte-identical (e2e-maps, e2e-planner, e2e-telemetry, e2e-toast, e2e-voice) and wl43 is largely contained in wl44. Deduplicating on (timestamp, disposition, item, mob) takes 1,866 loot lines down to 1,604 distinct events — a 14% inflation in every raw count the audit quoted. Conclusions are robust (disposition split, floor rule, gradient and ceiling all reproduce within a point), but the n's are not, and one finding turned on it outright: the "Efreeti War Club, twice" was one event at 22:59:58 appearing in two files. Every count in the surviving findings is now the deduplicated one, with the raw figure named where it differs.

KILLED OUTRIGHT.
1. The gust-of-wind hazard (old finding 14). This was our error and the most dangerous one in the set — it would have had the site publish a fictional zone hazard under TIER M. "A gust of wind" is not a hostile NPC. w52-cleave-lane.log line 1 reads `A gust of wind told you, 'Attacking an essence tamer Master.'` — it is the player's own pet, exactly the pet-announce pattern the audit itself used to unmask "Jenartik" and "Garab" two paragraphs earlier and then failed to apply here. The supporting claims collapse with it: "nothing ever damages one" is contradicted by `A gust of wind has been slain by Bzzazzt!` and `You have slain a gust of wind!` (and Bzzazzt is itself charmed, 22 times); the 46 kills it "landed" are the player's own kills through a pet; and the same reading disposes of "her two other deaths were landed by a thunder spirit" — `a thunder spirit has been charmed.` ×6 and `A thunder spirit told you, 'Attacking a thunder spirit Master.'`. Nothing survives that the site's existing "Damage to kill counts every attacker" caveat does not already cover.
2. The planner-array inference in the Orb of Tishan finding. The audit guessed that the hard-coded array in index-CZSHStxu.js was a "source unknown" list and offered to remove four entries from it. It is not. The bundle's own copy says: "Six Shadow Rage pieces are in this catalog because a live client holds them and the owner named the set. No source publishes their numbers, so this tool offers them by name under every slot they belong to and gives them no score at all", beside a counter labelled "offered by name, refused a rank". It is a no-published-stats list. Knowing where Orb of Tishan drops gives it no stats and takes nothing off that list. The measured drop survives; the inference is gone.
3. "Nine new set sources" (old finding 19), rewritten. The six-entry "Dropped by" lists are a truncation, not a total: 16 of 18 blocks show exactly six, while sightings.v1.json holds up to 15 mobs per set (Lustrous Russet 12, Rune Etched 15, Midnight Clad 15). Several of the proposed nine — "Lustrous Russet ← an abhorrent" among them — are already in the site's own data. Compared against the dataset instead of the display, the corpus adds 58 piece/mob pairs and 12 unsighted pieces; the finding is now about the missing hedge, which is the part that was right.
4. "A reader or tool holding a log cannot join it to a survey by any published field" (old finding 1), rewritten and downgraded from certain/high. False as stated: The Hole plate's own subtitle is "The Ruins of Old Paineel"; sightings.v1.json uses the client names throughout; /tools/faction-impact.html publishes the full client-name list with party tokens. The audit's "two of thirteen differ, the other eleven match" is also wrong — at least four differ (lowerguk, thehole, crushbone, mistmoore) and five surveys were never observed in our corpus at all, so eleven was never checkable. What remains is narrower and real: Lower Guk names it nowhere and zones.v1.json has no field for it.

NUMBERS CORRECTED IN PLACE, where the finding survived but the arithmetic did not: /items/ has 441 rows, not 440, and 441 = 435 items + 6 families, so the site's count is exactly right (I had implied it was loosely right); Najena 66, not 65; Solo/Group zone lines number 55 (52/3), not 53 (50/3); gust hits 105 not 106 and 14,619 damage not 14,864 (moot now); "created values reach +8" is understated — merges reach +8 in a log line and dumps hold +9; Orb of Tishan is two distinct events, not "twice" from one quoted line.

WHERE I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CALL THE SITE WRONG. The /items/ "435" count, the difficulty page's "about 12%" (measures 12.6%), the floor rule itself (0 violations in 459 drops), the Lord Nagafen measured row (a selection, not an inventory — Gauntlets of Fiery Might is in the site's own sightings and on the plate elsewhere), the island-7 Belt of Virtue listing (we did not see it; that is absence of evidence), and the /learn/difficulty zone-line examples (format illustrations, not transcripts). The three drop-attribution refusals the site publishes are genuine and I found no published rate whose denominator our pet/stranger-kill hazard could inflate.

STILL OPEN, honestly. The Thunder Spirit Princess damage-to-kill (her one player-credited kill is a fragment). Whether Key of the Misplaced gates anything. Whether Anthemion and Shadow Rage have a seventh slot. Whether +4 is a design cap or an artefact of D4 being the maximum tier — not separable from this corpus. Which measured body is which island (your open question 3): one /loc per island would also settle whether the soul/essence family is island-4 specific, which is the weakest joint in the zone-wide belt finding.

DATA READY TO HAND OVER, in your existing schemas: the 279 name→ID pairs for items.v1.json; the 459-row deduplicated tiered upgradeable-drop table behind the floor test; the full 1,604-row loot table with zone, party token, tier, mob, item, +N and disposition; the 58 new set piece/mob pairs against sightings.v1.json; and the Plane of Sky Awakened run parsed boss by boss.

findings.evidence: T2, and this REPLACES the audit's version, which was wrong in its central claim. (1) THE FORMULA IS NOT OURS. eqlwiki `Game_Mechanics`, last edited 11 August 2026, §"Working Legends Damage Bonus Formula" already publishes it verbatim: `Hand Modifier × max(Character Level, Weapon Damage) × (min(Weapon Delay, 50) / 40) × (Character Level / 100)`, Hand Modifier 0.8 one-handed / 1.1 two-handed, with 14 directly-observed in-game readings, the same `min(delay,50)` cap, the same main-hand-only rule ("The secondary hand receives no Main Hand Damage Bonus under the current working model") and the same open questions. The audit's "this formula closes that gap" and "before anyone had the formula" do not survive. (2) THE SOURCE THE SITE SAYS DOES NOT EXIST IS IN ITS OWN PROVENANCE TABLE. The planner's meta.json names `jmoyers/everquest-companion` @ d25455e, `src/main/data/items.json`, role "enrichment: … statsBlock …". At that pinned commit (8,645,674 bytes, matching the recorded size) 3 items carry `Dmg Bon`/`Dmg Bonus` inside `statsBlock`; at that repository's head fd5e5bb (27 Aug 2026, one day after the planner's 26 Aug build) 20 do. So the line is stale rather than wrong in principle, and refreshing the pin lets the planner print a SOURCED figure with a field citation instead of a derivation. (3) OUR 2H CONSTANT IS CONFIRMED FAR BETTER THAN WE CLAIMED, AND OUR 1H CONSTANT IS REFUTED. Testing B against all 19 `Dmg Bon:` statblocks at level 50: two-handers 6/6 exact under floor() (efreeti war axe 19.25→19, war staff 20.63→20, war maul 24.06→24, skycleaver 24.06→24, wind staff 24.75→24, zweihander 30.94→30), and a brute-force search shows the ONLY proportional constant satisfying all six is B/delay ∈ [0.6857, 0.6889), which contains our 1.10×50/80 = 0.6875. DAMAGE-CHAIN.md claims this on one reading (Skycleaver); it holds on six. One-handers: 0/13 exact, every row low by 1.4–13.8%, implied hand modifier 0.700–0.800 (mean 0.763), and no linear-in-delay constant fits all 13 under floor, round or ceil. Our 0.69 also fails 0/6 against eqlwiki's own directly-observed level-49 one-handed readings (delay 22/23/24/30/36/40 → 10/11/12/14/17/19), which its 0.8 fits 5/6. (4) The audit's own corroboration is misdescribed twice: Efreeti Standard is the conflict DAMAGE-CHAIN.md §11 already flags at −13.7%, not a corroboration, and it is `sl:['SECONDARY']` — an item that can never be main hand; and the audit's meta-note says "two client readings, both one-handed" when its finding text names one 2H and one 1H. (5) A useful pattern for the site: the two label conventions split the data. `Dmg Bon:` (19 rows) is internally consistent; `Dmg Bonus:` (Cudgel of the Fool 2H dly 52 → printed 40 vs 34.4 predicted; Silver Dagger of Destruction, Velious, 1H dly 20 → 6 vs 8.6) are both wild outliers. findings.proposedFix: RANK 2. Do not ship a derived figure. Do two cheaper, better-sourced things. (a) Refresh the `jmoyers/everquest-companion` pin and parse `Dmg Bon:` out of `statsBlock`; 19 items then carry a per-item damage bonus with a real field citation — exactly the site's method — and the §03 line becomes "absent for all but N items" rather than "no source carries it". (b) If a derived figure is wanted for the rest, cite eqlwiki Game_Mechanics §7.5 as the source rather than presenting it as new, use ITS hand modifiers (0.8 / 1.1, not our 0.69 / 1.10), print it at level 50 only, and carry its own caveat that the model "should not yet be described as the exact server formula". Also correct our side: DAMAGE-CHAIN.md's 1H HandMod 0.69 should be struck — it rests on two client windows (`Garduk`, `Arydryidriyorn`) for which no artefact exists anywhere in this repository or scratchpad, and it is contradicted by 13 statblock fields and 6 wiki observations that agree with 0.8. (1) Tremor's Overview reads "causing between 106 and 122 damage to as many as 24 others nearby" — 24, not the 25 our brief and DDD.md §1 both print. Earthquake's does read 25 ("up to 25 nearby creatures"). (2) Avalanche and Pogonip are not target caps and must not sit in a `cap` column beside Column of Lightning. Either you can hit the same mobs 3 times, you can hit 2 mobs twice each, or you can hit 4 mobs once each." That is a cap on hits across waves, a different mechanic. (3) Lightning Strike is also outdoors-gated — "This spell can hit at most 4 targets. Only castable outdoors." — so the outdoor gate is not unique to Lightning Blast as the audit implies. Gravity Flux's Overview also contains "Two different incompatible versions of this spell exists in game" and "Please confirm damage at various levels", and Avalanche's contains a mana-efficiency argument. It is a structured field whose contents are prose, so each number in it needs its own standing rather than inheriting the container's tier. A related and cleanly-verified scraping hazard from the same pass, worth publishing alongside: the eqlwiki Chords of Dissonance SPELL page's Spell Effects section reads "Decrease Hitpoints by 2 per tick", while the Bard CLASS page's spell table row reads "1: Decrease Hitpoints by 2 (L2) to 14 (L50) per tick". The level scaling exists only in the class-page table. A scraper reading spell pages gets the base value for all three Bard passive PB AE songs — 8/tick against 57/tick at level 50, a 7× error — and it is a general hazard, not a Bard quirk.
findings.proposedFix: RANK 6. A fifth dataset rather than a tool: `ae-caps.v1.json`, one row per AE spell at level ≤ 50, with SEPARATE columns for target cap, total-hits cap, wave count and indoor/outdoor gate — collapsing those into one `cap` field would flatten the rain-nuke distinction and publish a wrong number. Carry the verbatim description string on every row so a reader can see the prose the number came from, and mark unstated as unstated rather than uncapped, which is the same "a dry streak is a ceiling, not a zero" discipline the planner already applies. Fix Tremor to 24 in our own DDD.md §1 before sending anything. This does cross the /tools/index.html scope line, which is why it sits below the corrections rather than above them; a 34-row cap table is not spellbook diffing, but the owner may reasonably read it as the thin end.

findings.siteSays: "Melee DPS — Favours weapon ratio, Strength, Dexterity and Agility." (planner bundle). The page's own standard elsewhere: "41 per cent of the catalogue carries no source standing. That is the single most useful thing to know before trusting a comparison, and the planner says it about itself rather than leaving it to be discovered." (/tools/50-upgrades.html §02)
findings.evidence: M-derived, and downgraded from the audit's confidence after checking what it rests on. Verified in the bundle: the literal above; RATIO scored as upgraded damage over delay; cap-aware scoring at 510 for attributes and 1000 for saves; `weaponCounts` true only for PRIMARY and SECONDARY. RATIO is a defensible basis — under the measured chain, one-handers with equal ratio but different damage and delay differ by 1.1–2.0% in main-hand DPS, because B ∝ min(delay,50)/delay is flat below delay 50. The audit's exchange-rate arithmetic is internally consistent and I reproduced it: a main-hand RATIO unit is worth d(DPS)/d(DMG) × delay = 3.48 × 26 = 90.5 DPS, so normalising to RATIO 40 gives STR 0.342 × 40/90.5 = 0.151 against a shipped 1, and HASTE 1.499 × 40/90.5 = 0.663 against a shipped 2. Its offhand figure of 34.5 is also right and does not conflict with its own −23% elsewhere: 34.5 is a marginal (offhand swing share 0.88 × 1.4911 / 1.520 = 0.863) while −23% is a level difference caused by B being an additive main-hand-only constant. WHAT I COULD NOT STAND BEHIND, AND WHY THIS IS NOW ONLY PLAUSIBLE: the marginals are a single point — one trio, one gear level, one weapon pair — and the HASTE weight in particular is not a constant. Worn haste is max-not-sum (the planner already implements this correctly, `o > t.haste && (t.haste = o)`, and scores it cap-aware against existing haste), so Monsoon's HASTE 36 is worth a great deal to a character with no haste and exactly zero to one already wearing Renard's Belt of Quickness at 41 — the catalogue's ceiling. The audit's "Fangol 22% above all three" and its Spearman figure both depend on an unstated haste baseline and I could not reproduce them. Separately, whether STR converts to damage at all is unsettled inside this project's own files: EQUIPMENT-TRUTH.md §1 says a 255 STR cap would pin StrengthModifier at 120 and make STR gear worth nothing, then records a client panel reading INT 295 that contradicts the cap; the planner assumes 510; and eqlwiki Game_Mechanics adds `if STR < 75: StrengthModifier = 0`, a clause our chain omits.
findings.proposedFix: RANK 7. Ship it as a SECOND preset ("Melee DPS, measured") beside the existing one rather than replacing it, since the Weights tab already lets a user edit weights. Suggested, normalised to RATIO 40 on the main hand: RATIO 40 main / 34.5 offhand, STR 0.15, HASTE 0.66 — published as a band with its assumptions named (level 50, one trio, one weapon pair, and a stated haste baseline, because the haste weight is not scale-free). Mark DEX untested rather than zeroed: this session established procs are per-minute, but nothing tested whether DEX feeds that rate. And AGI, STA, AC and HP buy survivability, not damage — if that is the intent the preset is fine and only its label is wrong, and splitting it into "Melee DPS" and "Melee, all-round" costs nothing and is the smaller claim.
