findings.evidence: MOSTLY A CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT, WHICH PROPOSED SOMETHING ALREADY SHIPPED. The ladder matches this session's independent 66/66 solve from four /outputfile dumps exactly — the audit says this and it is right. But its proposed fix — "intersect the host's slot list with the donor's; if the result is empty, say the host becomes unwearable rather than silently totalling its stats" — is already implemented, and better than proposed. `Hr(donor, host)` returns false unless their slot lists intersect and their class lists intersect; `Ur(host, legalDonors)` narrows the host's class and slot lists by every legal donor; the UI prints "Donor restrictions narrow this item out of … slot X. Your active loadout can no longer use it." and, for the rejected ones, "N donors share no slot or class with the item holding them — the game would refuse the socket." Donor stats are never added to the sheet in any case: `Kt()` sums positions only. What survives is much smaller and I verified it on the planner's own catalogue: of 2,263 unique items across sh-*.json, 91 carry a `k:'proc'` combat effect and 91 of 91 sit on PRIMARY, SECONDARY or RANGE — zero on armour. So the Proc socket the planner opens at +4 on a bracer can never be legally filled by anything in its catalogue, and the player finds that out only after picking a donor. Our own weakest claim is unchanged and should be stated as such: the corpus holds exactly one slot-10 exaltation, `Primary-Slot10 Thelvorn, Blade of Light (Exaltation)`, so "armour proc sockets fire zero lanes" rests on mechanism plus a player report, corroborated only negatively (a spell-damage line falls within 1 s of an ordinary melee swing 20.9% of the time and within 1 s of an (Exaltation) message 16.9% — below chance; Golden Efreeti Boots 0 of 25).
findings.proposedFix: RANK 8, and much smaller than the audit made it. Two cheap touches, no new data: say at the socket rather than after the pick that no donor in the catalogue can legally fill a Proc socket on a non-weapon position (91/91 proc donors are weapon-slot-only), and print a "proc lanes: N" line on the character sheet — 1 on a two-hander, 2 dual-wielding, +1 on a Ranger bow — as a stated inference with its reasoning, in the site's usual voice. Do NOT re-propose the slot-intersection rule; the planner has it, and telling the owner otherwise would be the kind of error that costs the rest of this brief its credibility.

WHAT I KILLED, AND WHY.

KILLED OUTRIGHT — the haste finding (audit rank 9). This is the one that would have embarrassed us. The measurement reproduces perfectly: I re-parsed jos437-finishing-blow.log and got 439 slash attempts over 395 s engaged = 1.111 attempts/s, and a second, independent accounting (264 distinct slash timestamps, mean in-combat gap 1.49 s, 1.663 attempts per timestamp) gives the same round period of ~1.37 s. The CONCLUSION does not survive. The logging character is PAL/MNK/ENC — a Monk — and the Monk's autogranted `Unbound Alacrity` AA (EQBuddy AaCatalog.json, cost 0, maxRank 3, level 12/30/?) reads verbatim: "Gives a passive 3/6/10% increase in your current and maximum haste value." Applied to eqlwiki's 75% cap that gives 82.5% or 85% depending on whether the 10% is multiplicative or additive — an attack-speed multiplier of 1.825 or 1.85 against a measured 1.900, i.e. 4.1% or 2.7% away, comfortably inside the band that MH_CHAIN's own confidence interval [1.465, 1.569] opens (1.841–1.972). The audit compared against 1.75 only and called the cap "refuted... by a clear margin". Our own DAMAGE-CHAIN.md §8 already prints the correct comparison — "eqlwiki Haste Guide 75 (+10 Monk) | 1.85 | −2.7%" — and the audit dropped that line. The 75% cap is not refuted by this corpus. With the conclusion gone the finding has nothing left to offer the still-true entry, which is waiting on the unit question that this measurement does not touch either, so it goes rather than being downgraded.

KILLED — the trio damage model (audit rank 10). It names no site error, closes no gap, and is a recommendation not to build something. Its supporting numbers are the model's own self-assessment.
